source.text: וַיָּ֣חֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֤וֹת אֶת־בֵּית־יְהוָה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּהַר֙ הַמּ֣וֹרִיָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִרְאָ֖ה לְדָוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יהוּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵכִין֙ בִּמְק֣וֹם דָּוִ֔יד בְּגֹ֖רֶן אָרְנָ֥ן הַיְבוּסִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And began Solomon to build [the] house of Yahweh in Jerusalem on [the] mount of the Moriah, where he appeared to David his father, which he prepared in [the] place of David, on [the] threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

en.L: And Solomon began to build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had appeared to David his father, which he had prepared at the place of David, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
en.B: In Jerusalem, on Mount Moriah, Solomon began building the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It was there that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had appeared to his father David, at the site David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
en.R: Solomon began to build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah. That was where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had appeared to his father David. It was the place David had made ready, on the threshing floor that had belonged to Ornan the Jebusite. A threshing floor was a flat, open place where grain was beaten out.

decisions.choice: Mount Moriah: the temple hill, linked with the place where Abraham was sent to offer Isaac
decisions.reason: The name Moriah is found elsewhere only in Genesis 22:2, where God sent Abraham to "the land of Moriah" to offer Isaac on one of its mountains, and where God provided a ram in Isaac's place (Genesis 22:13-14). By calling the temple hill Mount Moriah, the writer ties the place of Israel's sacrifices to that mountain. Genesis itself speaks of a land with several mountains and does not name Jerusalem; the link is made here.

decisions.choice: the threshing floor of Ornan: the place of 1 Chronicles 21
decisions.reason: There the angel of Yahweh stood when the plague was stopped, David bought the threshing floor, built an altar, and Yahweh answered him with fire from heaven (1 Chronicles 21:15-26). David then said, "This is the house of Yahweh God" (1 Chronicles 22:1). 2 Samuel 24:16-25 tells the same story and spells the owner's name Araunah. 1 Kings 6:1, which this verse retells, does not name the site.

decisions.choice: where he had appeared: Yahweh appeared to David
alternatives: which had been shown to David
decisions.reason: The verb means "appeared" or "let himself be seen", and no subject is named. The one who appeared is Yahweh, whose answer came at this place (1 Chronicles 21:26; the same verb is used of God appearing to Solomon in 7:12). It could also be read "which had been shown to David", meaning the place itself.

decisions.choice: which he had prepared at the place of David: the place that David had prepared
alternatives: which he had prepared, at David's place
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word order is awkward: "which he prepared, in the place of David". The early Greek translation reads "in the place that David prepared", which is likely the sense: David chose and bought the site and made ready the materials for the temple (1 Chronicles 21:25-22:5). Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

decisions.choice: where the LORD had appeared
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the LORD as the one who appeared (m3); Literal keeps the bare verb with a pronoun.

decisions.choice: that had belonged to ...; A threshing floor was a flat, open place where grain was beaten out.
decisions.reason: David had bought the threshing floor from Ornan (1 Chronicles 21:25), so Readable says it had belonged to him, and explains the threshing floor as 2 Samuel 24:16 does. Balanced and Readable say "the house of the LORD" and "the temple of the LORD" as 1 Kings 6:1 does.

source.text: וַ֠יָּחֶל לִבְנ֞וֹת בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי֙ בַּשֵּׁנִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֖ע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he began to build in the month the second, on the second, in [the] year four of his reign.

en.L: And he began to build in the second month, on the second [day], in the fourth year of his reign.
en.B: He began to build in the fourth year of his reign, on the second day of the second month.
en.R: He started building in the fourth year that he was king, on the second day of the second month of the year, in spring.

decisions.choice: on the second: the second day of the month
alternatives: in the second month (without a day)
decisions.reason: The words "on the second" stand after "in the second month" with no word for "day", and some ancient translations do not have them. They may be a copying repeat of the word before them. Kept as the Hebrew text has them, they give the day of the month.

decisions.choice: in the fourth year of his reign: as 1 Kings 6:1
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 6:1 gives the same year and month, names the month Ziv, and dates the building from the exodus, the 480th year after Israel came out of Egypt. Chronicles gives only the year of Solomon's reign.

decisions.choice: on the second day of the second month
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the date in the usual English order and supply "day".

decisions.choice: of the year, in spring
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:1, Readable adds the season so that the month means something to the reader.

source.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֖וֹת אֶת־בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים הָאֹ֡רֶךְ אַמּ֞וֹת בַּמִּדָּ֤ה הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ אַמּ֣וֹת שִׁשִּׁ֔ים וְרֹ֖חַב אַמּ֥וֹת עֶשְׂרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] founding of Solomon to build the house of the God: the length, cubits by the measure the former, [was] cubits sixty, and [the] breadth cubits twenty.

en.L: And these [are] the foundation [measures] of Solomon for building the house of God: the length in cubits by the former measure [was] 60 cubits, and the breadth 20 cubits.
en.B: These are the measurements Solomon laid down for building the house of God: measured by the old standard, the length was {{units:about 90 feet|60 cubits}} and the width {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}}.
en.R: Here are the measurements Solomon used for the base of God's temple. Measured by the old standard, it was {{units:about 90 feet|60 cubits}} long and {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: the founding: the ground plan Solomon laid down
decisions.reason: The word is a rare form of the verb "to lay a foundation". Here it introduces the measurements of the base of the building, the plan on which it was founded.

decisions.choice: cubits by the former measure: the older, longer cubit
decisions.reason: A cubit was the length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, about 18 inches. There was also a longer cubit, "a cubit and a handbreadth" (Ezekiel 40:5), about 20 1/2 inches. The writer notes that the temple was measured by the older standard of Solomon's day, most likely this longer cubit. The modern measures here reckon 18 inches, as in 1 Kings 6:2, so the building may have been somewhat larger.

decisions.choice: sixty by twenty cubits: as 1 Kings 6:2
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 6:2 gives the same length and width and adds a height of 30 cubits, which Chronicles does not give.

decisions.choice: modern measures with the cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:2, Balanced and Readable give the size in feet, reckoning a cubit at about 18 inches; the reader's Measures control shows the cubits. Literal keeps the cubits throughout this chapter.

decisions.choice: the house of God (Balanced); God's temple (Readable); temple for "the house" alone
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6, Literal keeps "house" throughout. Balanced keeps "house" in the full phrases "the house of God" and "the house of the LORD" and says "temple" where "the house" names the building; Readable says "temple" throughout.

source.text: וְהָאוּלָ֡ם אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל־פְּנֵ֨י הָאֹ֜רֶךְ עַל־פְּנֵ֤י רֹֽחַב־הַבַּ֨יִת֙ אַמּ֣וֹת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְהַגֹּ֖בַהּ מֵאָ֣ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֑ים וַיְצַפֵּ֥הוּ מִפְּנִ֖ימָה זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the porch which [was] on [the] face, the length on [the] face of [the] breadth of the house [was] cubits twenty, and the height one hundred and twenty; and he overlaid it within [with] gold pure.

en.L: And the porch that [was] in front: its length, along the breadth of the house, [was] 20 cubits, and the height 120; and he overlaid it inside [with] pure gold.
en.B: The porch in front of the temple was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} long, matching the width of the temple, and {{units:about 180 feet|120 cubits}} high. He overlaid its inside with pure gold.
en.R: In front of the temple there was a porch. It ran {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} across the whole front of the temple, and it was {{units:about 180 feet|120 cubits}} high. Solomon covered the inside of it with pure gold.

decisions.choice: one hundred and twenty: the height of the porch as the Hebrew text gives it
decisions.reason: A porch 120 cubits high would rise four times above the 30-cubit house (1 Kings 6:2), and 1 Kings 6:3 gives the porch no height at all. Some copies of the early Greek translation and the Syriac translation read "twenty cubits", and the Hebrew words for "hundred" and "cubits" look alike, so "hundred" may have come from a misread "cubits". The Hebrew number is kept; if it is right, the porch was a tall tower at the entrance.

decisions.choice: the porch in front; its length along the breadth of the house
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:3, the porch is the entrance hall at the front of the temple. Its length of 20 cubits ran across the front, the same as the width of the house (verse 3). The Hebrew of this half of the verse is very compressed, and the porch's depth (10 cubits in 1 Kings 6:3) is not given.

decisions.choice: overlaid ... with pure gold
decisions.reason: The verb means to overlay or plate, as with the gold of the ark (Exodus 25:11) and of the inner room (1 Kings 6:20). "Pure" gold is refined gold.

decisions.choice: porch (all levels); overlaid (Literal, Balanced), covered (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:3 and 6:20.

source.text: וְאֵ֣ת׀הַבַּ֣יִת הַגָּד֗וֹל חִפָּה֙ עֵ֣ץ בְּרוֹשִׁ֔ים וַיְחַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָ֣ב ט֑וֹב וַיַּ֧עַל עָלָ֛יו תִּמֹרִ֖ים וְשַׁרְשְׁרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the house the great he covered [with] wood of cypresses, and he overlaid it [with] gold fine, and he put up on it palm trees and chains.

en.L: And the great house he covered [with] cypress wood, and he overlaid it [with] fine gold, and he set on it palm trees and chains.
en.B: He paneled the main hall with cypress wood and overlaid it with fine gold, and he decorated it with palm trees and chains.
en.R: He lined the walls of the main room with cypress wood and covered it with fine gold. Then he decorated it with designs of palm trees and chains.

decisions.choice: the great house: the main hall
decisions.reason: "The great house" is the large front room of the temple, 40 cubits long, in front of the most holy place (1 Kings 6:17), called "the hall" in 1 Kings 6:3.

decisions.choice: covered with cypress wood: 1 Kings 6:15 names cedar for the walls
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 6:15 says the walls were lined with cedar boards and the floor with cypress. Chronicles speaks only of cypress for the main hall. Cypress here is a tall evergreen tree from Lebanon (2:7), whose exact kind is not certain.

decisions.choice: set on it palm trees and chains: decorations in relief
decisions.reason: The verb means "to make go up", here to set designs on the gold-covered walls. Palm trees were carved on the walls (1 Kings 6:29); the chains may be a chain-like pattern of garlands, as on the pillars (verse 16; 1 Kings 6:21). "Fine" gold is literally "good" gold.

decisions.choice: covered (Literal), paneled (Balanced), lined the walls (Readable); the great house (Literal), the main hall (Balanced), the main room (Readable)
decisions.reason: With wood, the verb for covering means paneling, as in 1 Kings 6:15. Balanced and Readable name the room as 1 Kings 6:3 does.

source.text: וַיְצַ֧ף אֶת־הַבַּ֛יִת אֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָ֖ה לְתִפְאָ֑רֶת וְהַזָּהָ֖ב זְהַ֥ב פַּרְוָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he overlaid the house [with] stone precious for beauty; and the gold [was] gold of Parvaim.

en.L: And he overlaid the house [with] precious stone for beauty; and the gold [was] gold of Parvaim.
en.B: He adorned the temple with precious stones to make it beautiful, and the gold he used was gold from Parvaim.
en.R: He decorated the temple with precious stones to make it beautiful. The gold he used came from Parvaim.

decisions.choice: overlaid with precious stone: set with precious stones
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for overlaying with gold; with stones it means adorning the house by setting them in it. "Stone" stands for stones of every kind, which David had gathered for the temple (1 Chronicles 29:2). 1 Kings does not mention them.

decisions.choice: Parvaim: a place known for its gold, whose location is unknown
decisions.reason: The name is found only here. It is probably a land from which fine gold came, perhaps in Arabia, but it cannot be located, and it may instead name a kind or quality of gold.

decisions.choice: overlaid (Literal), adorned (Balanced), decorated (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb used for gold; Balanced and Readable use a verb that fits stones.

source.text: וַיְחַ֨ף אֶת־הַבַּ֜יִת הַקֹּר֧וֹת הַסִּפִּ֛ים וְקִֽירוֹתָ֥יו וְדַלְתוֹתָ֖יו זָהָ֑ב וּפִתַּ֥ח כְּרוּבִ֖ים עַל־הַקִּירֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he overlaid the house, the beams, the thresholds, and its walls and its doors, [with] gold; and he engraved cherubim on the walls.

en.L: And he overlaid the house, the beams, the thresholds and its walls and its doors, [with] gold; and he engraved cherubim on the walls.
en.B: He overlaid the temple with gold, its beams, its thresholds, its walls and its doors, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
en.R: He covered the temple with gold: the beams, the doorsteps, the walls and the doors. He carved cherubim on the walls. Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures.

decisions.choice: the house, the beams, the thresholds ...: the parts of the house that were overlaid
decisions.reason: The list after "the house" says which parts of it were covered with gold.

decisions.choice: cherubim: winged heavenly beings who guard God's presence
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:23. Cherubim guarded the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24) and stood over the ark (Exodus 25:18-22). 1 Kings 6:29 adds that palm trees and open flowers were carved with them.

decisions.choice: Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures.
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:23, Readable explains the word the first time it appears in the chapter.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת־בֵּֽית־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים אָרְכּ֞וֹ עַל־פְּנֵ֤י רֹֽחַב־הַבַּ֨יִת֙ אַמּ֣וֹת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְרָחְבּ֖וֹ אַמּ֣וֹת עֶשְׂרִ֑ים וַיְחַפֵּ֨הוּ֙ זָהָ֣ב ט֔וֹב לְכִכָּרִ֖ים שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made [the] house of [the] holy of the holies: its length on [the] face of [the] breadth of the house [was] cubits twenty, and its breadth cubits twenty; and he overlaid it [with] gold fine, to talents six hundred.

en.L: And he made the house of the holy of holies: its length, along the breadth of the house, [was] 20 cubits, and its breadth 20 cubits; and he overlaid it [with] fine gold, amounting to 600 talents.
en.B: He made the most holy place. Its length, matching the width of the temple, was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}}, and its width was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}}. He overlaid it with fine gold weighing {{units:about 45,000 pounds|600 talents}}.
en.R: He made the most holy place. It was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} long, the same as the width of the temple, and {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide. He covered it with {{units:about 45,000 pounds|600 talents}} of fine gold.

decisions.choice: the house of the holy of holies: the most holy place
decisions.reason: "Holy of holies" is the Hebrew way of saying "most holy" (Exodus 26:33). This is the inner room at the back of the temple where the ark stood (1 Kings 6:16, 19), called "the inner room" in verse 16.

decisions.choice: six hundred talents: about 45,000 pounds of gold
decisions.reason: A talent was about 75 pounds, so the gold weighed some twenty-two tons. The amount matches the great wealth told of Solomon, who received 666 talents of gold in one year (1 Kings 10:14).

decisions.choice: twenty cubits by twenty: as 1 Kings 6:20
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 6:20 gives the same length and width, adds a height of 20 cubits, and says the room was overlaid with pure gold without giving its weight.

decisions.choice: the house of the holy of holies (Literal); the most holy place (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 26:33 and 1 Kings 6:16.

decisions.choice: about 45,000 pounds, with 600 talents as the alternative
decisions.reason: A talent is reckoned at about 75 pounds; the reader's Measures control shows the talents.

source.text: וּמִשְׁקָ֛ל לְמִסְמְר֥וֹת לִשְׁקָלִ֖ים חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים זָהָ֑ב וְהָעֲלִיּ֖וֹת חִפָּ֥ה זָהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] weight for [the] nails, to shekels fifty, of gold; and the upper rooms he overlaid [with] gold.

en.L: And the weight for the nails [was] 50 shekels of gold; and the upper rooms he overlaid [with] gold.
en.B: The gold for the nails weighed {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds|50 shekels}}. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
en.R: He used {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds|50 shekels}} of gold for the nails. He also covered the upper rooms with gold.

decisions.choice: the weight for the nails: fifty shekels of gold
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say whether fifty shekels was the gold for all the nails or for each one. The nails may have been gold, or gold-covered nails that held the gold plating in place. 1 Kings does not mention them.

decisions.choice: the upper rooms: rooms above
decisions.reason: These were rooms on an upper level, perhaps above the most holy place, which was lower than the main building (1 Kings 6:2, 20), or upper rooms of the side building (1 Kings 6:5-6). David's plan for the temple also names them (1 Chronicles 28:11).

decisions.choice: about 1 1/4 pounds, with 50 shekels as the alternative
decisions.reason: A shekel is reckoned at about 2/5 ounce; the reader's Measures control shows the shekels.

source.text: וַיַּ֜עַשׂ בְּבֵֽית־קֹ֤דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ כְּרוּבִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה צַעֲצֻעִ֑ים וַיְצַפּ֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made in [the] house of [the] holy of the holies cherubim two, a work of sculpture, and they overlaid them [with] gold.

en.L: And he made in the house of the holy of holies two cherubim, sculptured work, and they overlaid them [with] gold.
en.B: He made two cherubim of sculptured work in the most holy place, and they were overlaid with gold.
en.R: In the most holy place he made two statues of cherubim, and they were covered with gold.

decisions.choice: a work of tsa'atsu'im: sculptured work
decisions.reason: The word tsa'atsu'im is found only here, and its meaning is uncertain. It is usually taken as carved or sculptured figures; others take it as cast metal work. 1 Kings 6:23 says the cherubim were made of olive wood, which fits carved figures overlaid with gold.

decisions.choice: they overlaid them: the workers overlaid them
decisions.reason: The verb is plural with no subject named; it means simply that the cherubim were overlaid with gold, as 1 Kings 6:28 says.

decisions.choice: two cherubim: 1 Kings 6:23-28
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 6:23 adds that each cherub was 10 cubits high; Chronicles gives only the length of their wings (verses 11-13).

decisions.choice: they were overlaid (Balanced); they were covered (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the unnamed "they" into a passive (m2); Readable says "statues" for the sculptured work.

source.text: וְכַנְפֵי֙ הַכְּרוּבִ֔ים אָרְכָּ֖ם אַמּ֣וֹת עֶשְׂרִ֑ים כְּנַ֨ף הָאֶחָ֜ד לְאַמּ֣וֹת חָמֵ֗שׁ מַגַּ֨עַת֙ לְקִ֣יר הַבַּ֔יִת וְהַכָּנָ֤ף הָאַחֶ֨רֶת֙ אַמּ֣וֹת חָמֵ֔שׁ מַגִּ֕יעַ לִכְנַ֖ף הַכְּר֥וּב הָאַחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] wings of the cherubim, their length [was] cubits twenty: [the] wing of the one, of cubits five, touching [the] wall of the house, and the wing the other, cubits five, touching [the] wing of the cherub the other.

en.L: And the wings of the cherubim, their length [was] 20 cubits: the wing of the one, of 5 cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing, 5 cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub.
en.B: The wings of the cherubim measured {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} in all. One wing of the first cherub, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} long, touched the wall of the temple, and its other wing, also {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}}, touched the wing of the second cherub.
en.R: Together the wings of the two cherubim reached {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}}. Each wing was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} long. One wing of the first cherub touched the temple wall, and its other wing touched a wing of the second cherub.

decisions.choice: their length twenty cubits: the four wings end to end
decisions.reason: Each cherub had two wings of five cubits, so the four wings together stretched twenty cubits, the full width of the most holy place (verse 8), as 1 Kings 6:24-27 also describes.

decisions.choice: the wing of the one: one wing of the first cherub
decisions.reason: "The one" is the first cherub; one of its wings touched the side wall and the other reached the second cherub's wing.

decisions.choice: in all; first ... second; Together ... two
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly which cherub is meant and that the twenty cubits are the wings together (m1, m2).

source.text: וּכְנַ֨ף הַכְּר֤וּב הָאֶחָד֙ אַמּ֣וֹת חָמֵ֔שׁ מַגִּ֖יעַ לְקִ֣יר הַבָּ֑יִת וְהַכָּנָ֤ף הָאַחֶ֨רֶת֙ אַמּ֣וֹת חָמֵ֔שׁ דְּבֵקָ֕ה לִכְנַ֖ף הַכְּר֥וּב הָאַחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] wing of the cherub the one, cubits five, touching [the] wall of the house, and the wing the other, cubits five, joined to [the] wing of the cherub the other.

en.L: And the wing of the one cherub, 5 cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing, 5 cubits, joined to the wing of the other cherub.
en.B: One wing of the second cherub, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} long, touched the other wall of the temple, and its other wing, also {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}}, met the wing of the first cherub.
en.R: In the same way, one wing of the second cherub touched the other side wall, and its other wing met a wing of the first cherub.

decisions.choice: the one cherub ... the other cherub: here the second cherub, then the first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not number the cherubim. In verse 11 "the one" is the first cherub; here the same words describe the second, whose inner wing meets the first cherub's wing. The other wall is the opposite side wall (1 Kings 6:27).

decisions.choice: joined to: meeting
decisions.reason: The word means "clinging" or "joined", a different word from "touching" in verse 11 but with the same sense: the inner wings met in the middle of the room.

decisions.choice: second ... first; the other wall; In the same way
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the cherubim and the wall as verse 11 and 1 Kings 6:27 make clear (m1). Readable does not repeat the five cubits given in verse 11.

source.text: כַּנְפֵי֙ הַכְּרוּבִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה פֹּֽרְשִׂ֖ים אַמּ֣וֹת עֶשְׂרִ֑ים וְהֵ֛ם עֹמְדִ֥ים עַל־רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם וּפְנֵיהֶ֥ם לַבָּֽיִת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] wings of the cherubim these [were] spreading out cubits twenty; and they [were] standing on their feet, and their faces toward the house.

en.L: The wings of these cherubim spread out 20 cubits; and they stood on their feet, and their faces [were] toward the house.
en.B: The wings of these cherubim spread out {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}}. They stood on their feet, facing the main hall.
en.R: The wings of these cherubim spread out {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}}. The cherubim stood on their feet and faced out toward the main room.

decisions.choice: standing on their feet: standing upright on the floor
decisions.reason: Unlike the two small cherubim of the tabernacle, which were part of the ark's cover (Exodus 25:18-20), these large figures stood on the floor of the room, with the ark beneath their wings (5:7-8).

decisions.choice: their faces toward the house: facing out toward the main hall
decisions.reason: "The house" here is the main part of the building in front of the most holy place (verse 5). The cherubim faced out toward the entrance, not toward each other as the cherubim on the ark did (Exodus 25:20).

decisions.choice: facing the main hall (Balanced); faced out toward the main room (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the room meant by "the house" (m2).

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת־הַפָּרֹ֔כֶת תְּכֵ֥לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֖ן וְכַרְמִ֣יל וּב֑וּץ וַיַּ֥עַל עָלָ֖יו כְּרוּבִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he made the veil [of] violet and purple and crimson and fine linen, and he put up on it cherubim.

en.L: And he made the veil of blue and purple and crimson [yarn] and fine linen, and he worked cherubim on it.
en.B: He made the inner curtain of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen, and worked cherubim into its design.
en.R: He made the inner curtain from blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen, and he had cherubim woven into it.

decisions.choice: the veil: the curtain before the most holy place
decisions.reason: This word is used of the curtain that shut off the most holy place in the tabernacle (Exodus 26:31-33), made of the same colors with cherubim worked into it.

decisions.choice: the veil: 1 Kings speaks of doors
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 6:31-32 describes doors of olive wood at the entrance of the inner room, and does not mention a veil. Chronicles names a veil like the tabernacle's, and later also mentions doors of the inner house (4:22). There may have been both: the gold chains drawn across the front of the inner room (1 Kings 6:21) may have held a curtain.

decisions.choice: crimson; fine linen: later words for the tabernacle's scarlet and linen
decisions.reason: The word for crimson is found only in Chronicles (2:6, 13), and the word for fine linen is a later word than the one in Exodus. They name the same costly dyed yarn and linen.

decisions.choice: put up on it cherubim: worked cherubim into it
decisions.reason: The verb "made go up" is the one used in verse 5: the figures were set into the fabric, as on the tabernacle veil, which was "the work of a skilled craftsman" (Exodus 26:31).

decisions.choice: the veil (Literal); the inner curtain (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 26:31.

decisions.choice: [yarn] (Literal); yarn (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the colors only; English needs the noun, as in Exodus 26:31.

source.text: וַיַּ֜עַשׂ לִפְנֵ֤י הַבַּ֨יִת֙ עַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם אַמּ֕וֹת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְחָמֵ֖שׁ אֹ֑רֶךְ וְהַצֶּ֥פֶת אֲשֶׁר־עַל־רֹאשׁ֖וֹ אַמּ֥וֹת חָמֵֽשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he made before the house pillars two, cubits thirty and five [in] length; and the capital which [was] on its top, cubits five.

en.L: And he made in front of the house two pillars, 35 cubits [in] length; and the capital that [was] on its top [was] 5 cubits.
en.B: In front of the temple he made two pillars {{units:about 52 feet|35 cubits}} long, each with a capital {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} high on top.
en.R: He made two pillars to stand in front of the temple. They measured {{units:about 52 feet|35 cubits}}. On top of each one was a capital, a decorated top piece {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: thirty-five cubits: 1 Kings 7:15 has eighteen
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:15, 2 Kings 25:17 and Jeremiah 52:21 give each pillar a height of eighteen cubits. Here the word is "length", not height, and the number may be the two pillars together (eighteen and eighteen, near thirty-five), the length of the bronze as it was cast, or a difference that arose in copying, since numbers could be written with letters that are easily confused. The reason for the difference is not known.

decisions.choice: the capital: the crowning piece on top of each pillar
decisions.reason: The word for capital here is found only in this verse; 1 Kings 7:16 uses another word. Both name the large decorated top of each pillar, five cubits high in both books. "Its top" means the top of each pillar.

decisions.choice: long (Balanced); measured (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "length", not "height", so Balanced and Readable do not say how the pillars were measured (m1).

decisions.choice: a decorated top piece
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:16, Readable explains the building word "capital".

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ שַׁרְשְׁרוֹת֙ בַּדְּבִ֔יר וַיִּתֵּ֖ן עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָעַמֻּדִ֑ים וַיַּ֤עַשׂ רִמּוֹנִים֙ מֵאָ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן בַּֽשַּׁרְשְׁרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made chains in the inner room, and he put [them] on [the] top of the pillars; and he made pomegranates one hundred, and he put [them] on the chains.

en.L: And he made chains in the inner room and put [them] on the top of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates and put [them] on the chains.
en.B: He made chains in the inner sanctuary and put them on top of the pillars. He also made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
en.R: He made chains in the inner room and put them on the tops of the pillars. He also made a hundred pomegranates and hung them on the chains.

decisions.choice: chains in the inner room: as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The pillars stood outside, in front of the temple, so chains "in the inner room" are puzzling. A change of one letter gives "like a necklace", describing chains set around the tops of the pillars like a necklace. The phrase may also mean chains like those in the inner room (1 Kings 6:21). The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: a hundred pomegranates: 1 Kings 7:20 and 7:42
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:18-20 describes wreaths of chain work and two rows of pomegranates on each capital, two hundred on each, four hundred in all (1 Kings 7:42). Jeremiah 52:23 speaks of a hundred on the network all around. The hundred here may be a row or the count on one pillar.

decisions.choice: pomegranates: bronze fruit as ornaments
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:18, pomegranates were a sign of the land's fruitfulness (Deuteronomy 8:8).

decisions.choice: the inner room (Literal, Readable); the inner sanctuary (Balanced)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:16 and 6:19.

source.text: וַיָּ֤קֶם אֶת־הָֽעַמּוּדִים֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַהֵיכָ֔ל אֶחָ֥ד מִיָּמִ֖ין וְאֶחָ֣ד מֵֽהַשְּׂמֹ֑אול וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם־הַיְמָנִי֙ יָכִ֔ין וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשְּׂמָאלִ֖י בֹּֽעַז׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he set up the pillars on [the] face of the temple, one from [the] right and one from the left; and he called [the] name of the right [one] Jachin, and [the] name of the left [one] Boaz.

en.L: And he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left; and he called the name of the right [one] Jachin and the name of the left [one] Boaz.
en.B: He erected the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and the other on the left. The pillar on the right he named Jachin, and the pillar on the left he named Boaz.
en.R: He put up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right side and one on the left. He named the pillar on the right Jachin, which means "He establishes", and he named the pillar on the left Boaz, which may mean "In him is strength".

decisions.choice: Jachin: "he establishes" or "he will establish"
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:21. The name is a verb form meaning "he makes firm"; the one who establishes is probably Yahweh, who promised to establish David's house and throne (1 Chronicles 17:11-14).

decisions.choice: Boaz: probably "in him is strength"
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:21. The meaning of this name is less clear; it is usually explained as "in him (or it) is strength". Boaz is also the name of David's ancestor (Ruth 4:21-22).

decisions.choice: in front of the temple: 1 Kings 7:21 has "at the porch of the temple"
decisions.reason: Both books name the pillars the same way and place Jachin on the right and Boaz on the left. 1 Kings 7:21 sets them at the porch; Chronicles says in front of the temple. The word for temple here names the main hall, before which the porch stood (1 Kings 6:3).

decisions.choice: the right one: the written and read forms differ in spelling
decisions.reason: The written text and the form read aloud differ slightly in the spelling of "the right one"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: which means "He establishes"; which may mean "In him is strength"
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:21, Readable gives the likely meanings of the names; the second is marked "may" because its sense is less certain (m2).

decisions.choice: erected (Balanced); set up (Literal); put up (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:21.
